basis: The envelopes the speed gate judges. Each population's `entries` record a deterministic statement count (`metric`: sys.monitoring LINE events in the measured Python child, Python 3.12+) as an observed min/max/n envelope, and `wall` records a gross elapsed-time smoke envelope. Measured in the speed job on the CPython `interpreter` names, the same code over the same collected population executes nearly the same lines on any runner, and its rounds differ by far less than `tolerance`. So `tolerance` covers only that spread, and a head value fails above its entry's max x (1 + `tolerance`). The count covers the direct child's own lines; nested Python children and non-Python subprocesses (the renderers' git calls) are left to the wall smoke bound. `population` is the sha256 of the collected node ids: the unit suite's from `compare_counters.py --print-population tests`, which `population_digest.py --write` re-derives in place, the renderers' from `e2e_bench.py --list-workloads`. A run over a different population is refused, not compared. Automation only lowers a maximum: a passing main push lowers any max it beats, and `seeds` names the entry ids the ratchet may seed. A unit-suite raise needs a feat subject in the judged window, and a renderer `entries` raise is admitted only across an `interpreter` move (CONTRIBUTING.md). `measured_commit` and `measured_at` name the tree and date of the last hand re-derivation, and `cell` names where the `wall` envelopes were observed.
